summary: Iter 118 backend validated via new pytest suite test_iter118_bugfixes.py (10 tests, 100% pass on first run). Feature A (tag-blocked rejection on POST) works end-to-end: A→B tag after A blocks B returns HTTP 400 with detail 'Non puoi taggare @chatUserB: c’è un blocco tra voi.' — verified for both comment endpoint and reply endpoint, symmetric block direction, case-insensitive nickname match (@CHATUSERB) with canonical DB-cased nickname surfaced in error, mixed valid+blocked mention correctly all-or-nothing rejects, plain-text with no mention still 200, unblock+retry succeeds and mention resolves. Feature B (existing-mention scrub, iter117 regression) also passes: A's pre-block comment tagging @chatUserB is scrubbed to '[utente bloccato]' and mentions[] no longer includes B; bi-directional (B fetches same behaviour); after unblock the raw @chatUserB and mention are restored. Iter117 (30 tests) + iter116 (5 tests) + iter115 (5 tests) regression: 29/30 pass. The 1 iter115 failure (test_mention_from_blocked_user_hidden) is a DELIBERATE spec supersession by iter118 — that test tried to POST a comment tagging a blocked user and expected 200 (then checked no notification was emitted); iter118 now rejects the POST with 400 upstream, which is strictly stronger than the iter115 assertion. Test needs updating to expect 400 instead of 200 (or be replaced by iter118 coverage). No other regressions detected.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py:5502-5581 (_resolve_mentions with raise_on_blocked) — implementation is correct and minimal. The canonical nickname is fetched via a bounded find({user_id: uid}).limit(1) which is fine but happens inside the loop; if a comment mentions 20 blocked users the current code short-circuits on the first hit (blocked_nick_hit is only set once) so the extra roundtrip is O(1) not O(N). Good.

server.py:3243 (add_comment) and server.py:3386 (add_reply) — both correctly pass raise_on_blocked=True. Both paths run AI moderation BEFORE _resolve_mentions, which is fine but means an AI moderation call is spent on a comment that will be rejected on mention grounds. Micro-opt (not required): swap the order so cheap mention resolution runs before the AI call. Impact is minor (blocked-mention posts are rare) and swapping would slightly weaken the moderation trail for flagged content. Leave as-is.

The error message hardcodes 'Non puoi taggare @{nick}: c’è un blocco tra voi.' — good UX (Italian, actionable, names the offender). Consider extracting the string to a constant if it needs i18n later.
Symmetric block check via _blocked_ids_for(author_id) — verified this returns the bi-directional union (blocks I made + blocks against me). Both directions are covered by a single call. No leak.

rca_of_issue: No new bug found. The iter115 test failure is a test-code staleness issue introduced by the deliberate spec change in iter118 (POST-level rejection replaces silent notification-suppression). Reproduction: `pytest /app/backend/tests/test_iter115_bugfixes.py::TestNotificationsBlockFilter::test_mention_from_blocked_user_hidden -v` → 400 vs expected 200 at line 504.
